extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of political philosophy; legislators and educators interested in the formation of philosopher-rulers (Plato's Republic)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and educational programme for producing the ideal guardian/philosopher-ruler: intellectual, moral, and pedagogical requirements (tests, studies, stages of learning, and obligations to govern).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians must be lovers of their country and tested by pleasures and pains
rubrics_metrics.description: They were to be lovers of their country, tried by the test of pleasures and pains, and neither in hardships, nor in dangers, nor at any other critical moment were to lose their patriotism—he was to be rejected who failed, but he who always came forth pure, like gold tried in the refiner’s fire, was to be made a ruler, and to receive honours and rewards in life and after death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use severe trials of pleasure/pain, hardship and danger as selection criteria; reject those who fail such tests; reward and honour those who remain pure under trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: The perfect guardian must be a philosopher
rubrics_metrics.description: The perfect guardian must be a philosopher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophic nature (love of wisdom and pursuit of highest knowledge) is a necessary defining quality for rulers of the ideal state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possession of combined intellectual gifts and steadfast temperament
rubrics_metrics.description: Quick intelligence, memory, sagacity, cleverness, and similar qualities do not often grow together with high-spiritedness and magnanimity; steadfast natures which can be depended upon are apt to be torpid intellectually. Yet both qualities were necessary in those to whom the higher education is to be imparted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select individuals who combine sharp intellectual faculties (memory, sagacity, quickness) with steadiness, courage, and the capacity to endure disciplined life; recognize that these traits rarely co-occur and must be balanced in selection and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing in many kinds of knowledge to endure the highest
rubrics_metrics.description: The aspirant must be exercised also in many kinds of knowledge, to see whether the soul will be able to endure the highest of all, or will faint under them, as in any other studies and exercises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expose candidates to a broad curriculum and progressively more demanding intellectual work to assess their capacity to bear and pursue highest studies (culminating in dialectic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Take the longer circuit: combine intellectual study with gymnastics
rubrics_metrics.description: The guardian then must be required to take the longer circuit, and toil at learning as well as at gymnastics, or he will never reach the highest knowledge of all which... is his proper calling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design an extended programme that integrates rigorous physical training with long-term intellectual study; avoid shortcuts—complete, sustained education is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of the form/idea of the Good is the highest and necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: The idea of good is the highest knowledge, and that all other things become useful and advantageous only by their use of this... without which, any other knowledge or possession of any kind will profit us nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that education culminates in comprehension of the Good (the supreme principle); possession of other virtues or knowledge is insufficient without this supreme insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress through four levels: images, belief, understanding, reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Corresponding to the divisions (visible/intelligible and their subdivisions) let there be four faculties in the soul—reason answering to the highest, understanding to the second, faith (or conviction) to the third, and perception of shadows to the last—and let there be a scale of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure learning so pupils move from perception of images (shadows/reflections) through belief and understanding (mathematical/hypothetical sciences) to reason (dialectic). Match pedagogical methods to these levels and their differing clearness/truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialectic: ascent beyond hypotheses to first principles
rubrics_metrics.description: In the higher of the intelligible divisions, the soul passes out of hypotheses, and goes up to a principle which is above hypotheses... using the hypotheses not as first principles, but only as hypotheses—that is to say, as steps and points of departure into a world which is above hypotheses, in order that she may soar beyond them to the first principle of the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train candidates in dialectical reasoning that uses mathematical/hypothetical knowledge as stepping-stones to grasp first principles; dialectic is the defining intellectual method for the highest knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation by geometry and cognate sciences (use of hypotheses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students of geometry, arithmetic, and the kindred sciences assume the odd and the even and the figures and three kinds of angles and the like... they make use of the visible forms and reason about them, they are thinking not of these, but of the ideals which they resemble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include rigorous training in geometry and related arts as preparatory disciplines—these cultivate understanding by working from sensible figures toward intelligible ideals and serve as intermediate steps toward dialectic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gradual acclimation to truth (allegory of the cave)
rubrics_metrics.description: A liberated prisoner, when compelled to turn toward the light, will suffer sharp pains... he will require to grow accustomed to the sight of the upper world: first he will see the shadows best, next reflections, then objects, then moon/stars, and last of all he will be able to see the sun and contemplate him as he is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement a staged, gradual exposure to increasing intellectual truth: begin with more accessible images and mathematical objects and progressively accustom the mind to the brightest truths to avoid overwhelming and to produce genuine comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Those who attain the highest knowledge must be compelled to descend and govern
rubrics_metrics.description: When they have ascended and seen enough we must not allow them to remain in the upper world; they must be made to descend again among the prisoners in the den, and partake of their labours and honours... the legislator did not aim at making any one class in the State happy above the rest; the happiness was to be in the whole State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require philosopher-rulers, once educated, to return to public life and serve the polis; enforce civic duty so the common good is prioritized over personal contemplative happiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulers should be disinclined to rule; govern as reluctant duty
rubrics_metrics.description: The State in which the rulers are most reluctant to govern is always the best and most quietly governed... each of you, when his turn comes, must go down to the general underground abode, and get the habit of seeing in the dark... they will take office as a stern necessity, and not after the fashion of our present rulers of State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor rulers who do not crave office for personal gain but accept governance as a burdensome duty; design incentives and cultural structures that cultivate reluctance to seek power and ensure ruling for the common good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-discipline and renunciation of sensual pleasures
rubrics_metrics.description: If there had been a circumcision of such natures in the days of their youth; and they had been severed from those sensual pleasures, such as eating and drinking, which... drag them down and turn the vision of their souls upon the things that are below—if they had been released from these impediments and turned in the opposite direction, the very same faculty in them would have seen the truth as keenly as they see what their eyes are turned to now.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impose early habits of temperance and restraint (renouncing sensual indulgences) so that natural intellectual capacities are freed to pursue higher truths rather than being tethered to bodily appetites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of education is required; neither uneducated nor permanently contemplative are fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the uneducated and uninformed of the truth, nor yet those who never make an end of their education, will be able ministers of State; not the former, because they have no single aim of duty... nor the latter, because they will not act at all except upon compulsion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure candidates complete the full curriculum (including dialectic) but also cultivate readiness to act responsibly in public life; avoid appointing the wholly untrained or the permanently aloof theoreticians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral orientation of intellect: ensure intelligence serves the good
rubrics_metrics.description: The virtue of wisdom more than anything else contains a divine element which always remains, and by this conversion is rendered useful and profitable; or, on the other hand, hurtful and useless. Did you never observe the narrow intelligence flashing from the keen eye of a clever rogue—how eager he is... he is mischievous in proportion to his cleverness?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guard against highly capable minds being directed toward selfish or malicious ends; moral cultivation must accompany intellectual training so cleverness is harnessed to the good rather than to mischief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and compulsion: the legislator must bind the best minds to public service
rubrics_metrics.description: You must contrive for your future rulers another and a better life than that of a ruler, and then you may have a well-ordered State... Wherefore each of you, when his turn comes, must go down to the general underground abode, and get the habit of seeing in the dark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a combination of persuasion, institutional design and obligation to ensure the best-educated serve the polity; create a structure in which rulers accept service out of duty and recognition of a higher life of wisdom rather than for private advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing by labours, dangers and pleasures (probation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Then the aspirant must not only be tested in those labours and dangers and pleasures which we mentioned before, but there is another kind of probation which we did not mention—he must be exercised also in many kinds of knowledge...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine practical probations (labours, dangers, temptations of pleasure) with intellectual examinations to ensure both moral steadiness and cognitive endurance before granting ruling responsibilities.
